item.title: New Steam Update Adds Long-Requested Feature
item.description:
A brand-new update to Steam has added new features for gifting games, fulfilling a long-standing request from the userbase. This is just the latest in recent changes to Steam's game gifting options in recent months.

Previously, Steam announced it would be discontinuing physical Steam gift cards. Though fans may still be able to find some in stores, once they run out of stock, they will no longer be produced and sold. The change was made in an effort to crack down on scams connected to gift cards targeting Steam users. Gamers can still buy and send Steam gift cards digitally, or they can use some of these new features to make gifting easier.

Steam Users Can Claim Co-Op Game Completely Free of Charge (Until It's Gone)

A limited-time, limited-supply deal lets Steam users claim a popular co-op game with 95% Overwhelmingly Positive reviews at no cost.

By Joshua Duckworth

Steam Makes Big Changes to Gifting Games

In a new update to Steam, the platform has made some changes to gifting that should make it much easier for gamers to get the gifts they want. In short, Steam users can now share their wishlists with others, who can then buy any of the games listed without the gifter needing a membership to the platform themselves. Games can now be gifted across regions, and gamers can be given digital gift cards for Steam without the sender needing to know their account information. All that will be needed from this point on is an email address of the user, and it doesn't have to be the email address associated with the account. This should help non-gamers to more easily buy gifts on Steam, and may help to increase privacy for users requesting gifts.

In addition to the changes to gifting, some smaller alterations have been made to wishlists themselves. Steam users can now organize wishlists into separate categories, and when sending the wishlist to another person, one can choose to just send a single category. For example, one might send a wishlist category with only educational games or a birthday wishlist to another person, while keeping the rest of their wishlist separate. This should ensure that any games a user places on their wishlist that they don't want others to know about will be kept private.

Since their inception, Steam wishlists have been an extremely handy way to give friends on the platform presents. If left public, users can browse their friends' wishlists and purchase a game right off it that will promptly be added to their account, providing a convenient way to give gifts on the fly. Combined with the already-existing ability to buy a game now and gift it at a later date, there are now considerable options for giving PC gamers what they want without having the gifter go through any significant hassles.

item.title: 7 Long Open-World RPGs That Take Forever To Complete, Ranked
item.description:
Traditionally, open-world RPGs are some of the longest games there are, requiring real dedication from players. What’s more, in many cases the base game is just the beginning. Going for the fullest editions available to experience absolutely everything the title has to offer can easily stretch to over 200 hours, resulting in months of intense play before finally rolling the credits.

For this list, I decided to focus on the fullest editions of some of the longest open-world RPGs available that can take forever to beat, ranking them by playtime. I use the “ Main+Extra ” figures from HowLongToBeat for each, as this is the most reliable metric for the average time people spend with these games. Almost no one focuses exclusively on the main story path, but they also rarely strive to do absolutely everything for 100% completion.

That said, the referenced data may not align perfectly with your experience, and it may take considerably longer depending on your playstyle, so keep that in mind. In my experience, it usually takes me up to 50 hours longer to clear open-world games like the ones listed below.

150 hours sounds huge, but what does this actually mean? For reference, you can play a game daily in 5-hour sessions for a whole month, or almost two months if you can’t afford more than 3 hours a day.

1 The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 150

Features:

  • The Witcher 3 - 100 hours
  • Hearts of Stone - 15 hours
  • Blood and Wine - 30 hours
  • Smaller Free DLC (including extra quests) - 3 hours
  • Songs of the Past - TBA

A pretty rare case in the industry, the so-called “Complete Edition” for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt turned out incomplete years later. With the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion on the horizon, one of the longest games of its genre is about to become even bigger. CDPR has already teased that the game’s third expansion will be in line with what fans have grown to expect from the studio’s past works, like Blood and Wine or Phantom Liberty .

Top Upcoming Open-World Games Releasing In August 2026

August isn’t as dry a month for open-world fans as it might seem — here are some promising new titles and long-awaited platform ports coming soon.

1
By Vlad Mazanko

Nevertheless, even without Songs of the Past , which will probably add 20 to 30 hours of playtime, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition is a colossal offering, almost unmatched in the industry to this day. What’s best, it’s also an extremely rare case where the quantity of content is matched by its quality, as both the Hearts of Stone and Blood & Wine expansions are considered some of the best additions of all time.

2 Assassin’s Creed Valhalla - Complete Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 145

Features:

  • AC Valhalla - 100 hours
  • Wrath of the Druids - 15 hours
  • The Siege of Paris - 10 hours
  • Dawn of Ragnarök - 15 hours
  • Smaller Free DLC (including extra quests) - 5 hours

If there’s a game that came the closest to The Witcher 3’s grand scope, it’s Assassin’s Creed Valhalla , boasting the biggest post-launch support among Ubisoft open-world titles to date. AC Valhalla received three substantial expansions, with Dawn of Ragnarök even released outside of the Season Pass due to the game’s enormous success. If only AC Shadows got more post-launch content rather than just one Claws of Awaji DLC.

6 Open-World Games Officially Longer Than Any Assassin's Creed Game

Odyssey and Valhalla rank among the biggest Assassin's Creed titles to date, but these massive open-world games are even longer.

15
By Vlad Mazanko

While AC Valhalla is often criticized for the base game’s bloat, featuring several explorable maps that are way too huge for their own good and a main story that suffers as a result of largely separate story arcs for each region, the expansions turned out to be a pleasant surprise. They strike just the right balance between the size of the new regions and the density of quests and activities. Wrath of the Druids is my personal favorite, with its mystical atmosphere, menacing foes, and a strong story that’s easy to stay invested in thanks to its memorable characters.

3 Elden Ring Tarnished Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 140

Features:

  • Elden Ring - 100 hours
  • Shadow of the Erdtree - 40 hours

Technically not available just yet, Tarnished Edition is a fancy title for a bundle that includes Elden Ring and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, both of which have been available to fans outside of Nintendo platforms for over two years now. Easily one of the best and biggest games of this entire generation, Elden Ring stands as comparable to The Witcher 3’s achievement in the open-world genre, perfectly placing the highlights of soulslike games into one of the most interesting and beautiful seamless maps to explore.

Despite the undeniable breadth of content on offer, SOTE still has a somewhat mixed reputation. It has been criticized for its overtuned difficulty in some boss encounters, the questionable Scadutree mechanics that can slow down subsequent runs, and the lack of a proper ending that some players expected. To me though, there are no real issues here. I’d vote Shadow of the Erdtree the best and biggest story expansion ever made — yes, even better than Blood and Wine .

4 The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim - Special Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 140

Features:

  • Skyrim - 110 hours
  • Dawnguard - 10 hours
  • Hearthfire - 5 hours
  • Dragonborn - 15 hours

Actually the oldest game among these, The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim still stands strong over the years, firmly remaining among the longest and most-played open-world titles of all time. Still considered Bethesda’s magnum opus, Skyrim has been re-released countless times on almost every platform imaginable since 2011. While the company recently reaffirmed active development of The Elder Scrolls 6 , it sounds like the game is still pretty far away — meaning it’s time for yet another Skyrim playthrough.

The Elder Scrolls 5 Skyrim: The 20 Wildest Things You Can Actually Do In-Game

Werewolves, cliff-diving, destroying love triangles... Skyrim is a playground where the Dragonborn can do all sorts of wild things.

By Anastasia Maillot

Skyrim has enjoyed the pretty standard post-launch support expected of its kind, offering two sizable story expansions with new regions such as Solstheim, and a smaller one, Hearthfire , mostly focused on the game’s leisure side, like acquiring land and building houses. Given how often Bethesda has updated the title, it would definitely be interesting to see more story content added over the years, like CDPR is doing now with The Witcher 3 . As it stands, mods remain the only real source of new quests and fresh content for the game’s long-term fans.

5 Assassin’s Creed Odyssey - Ultimate Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 130

Features:

  • AC Odyssey - 85 hours
  • Legacy of the First Blade - 10 hours
  • The Fate of Atlantis - 25 hours
  • The Lost Tales of Greece (free extra quests) - 10 hours

Before AC Valhalla took the helm as the biggest and longest game in the series, that title belonged to Assassin’s Creed Odyssey , which also received admirable post-launch support. Years after its release, playing the game in all its glory is even more fun — not just due to Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey movie event of the year that might inspire some to give it a go, but also thanks to all the expansions now being available as a complete package. Back in the day, their episodic launch nature was something I personally wasn’t a fan of.

As a whole, AC Odyssey is often hailed as the best RPG offering in the series. It features over 50 hours of extra content and several new explorable worlds added through its expansions and free updates, including small quests and the game’s ending chapter that ties Kassandra’s (or Alexios’) legacy into the overarching Assassin’s Creed franchise lore. AC Odyssey is best enjoyed in shorter sessions to prevent burnout, yet its gorgeous world and lighthearted mood can easily win you over for a mostly uninterrupted epic journey through every corner of Ancient Greece.

6 Fallout 4: Game of the Year Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 130

Features:

  • Fallout 4 - 85 hours
  • Automatron - 5 hours
  • Far Harbor - 15 hours
  • Nuka-World - 15 hours
  • Workshops DLC ( Vault-Tec , Contraptions , Wasteland ) - 10 hours

After Skyrim , Fallout 4 is probably Bethesda’s biggest accomplishment in terms of raw size and the wealth of post-launch DLC. With a map substantially smaller than Fallout 76’s , F4 offers much greater density, featuring vast urban regions of Boston and Cambridge built on layered exploration, countless dungeons, and multi-story buildings. It’ll be interesting to see how Fallout 5 will differ from the previous games. The sequel is already technically announced but is probably still years away, coming after TES 6 .

8 FPS Games That Are Basically Fallout With Great Gameplay

These FPS games capture the essence of what makes Fallout special, with great gameplay that's perfect for fans of Bethesda's franchise.

By Evan Regan

When compared to Skyrim , Fallout 4 offers less story-driven content for true adventurers and much more sandbox-style play. Its robust building and crafting mechanics let you put nearly every piece of junk you find in the Wasteland to good use. Some of the game’s DLC are entirely workshop-focused, adding new enhancements to the already in-depth construction system and allowing fans to sink dozens more hours into the game if they choose. Note that there’s also the newer (and usually more expensive) Fallout 4 - Anniversary Edition , with the only real difference being the addition of over 150 Creation Club items.

7 Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 Royal Edition

Hours of Play on Average: 130

Features:

  • KCD 2 - 100 hours
  • Brushes with Death - 7 hours
  • Legacy of the Forge - 15 hours
  • Mysteria Ecclesiae - 7 hours

After the original KCD that took quite some time and work to reach iconic status, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is an instant hit. There’s virtually no competition for such an immersive medieval open-world experience, so stepping into the shoes of Henry of Skalitz feels quite literally like starting another life. KCD2 is often hailed as The Witcher 3 or Skyrim of the current generation, standing as a true must-play for any RPG lover out there who values story, characters, and plausibility of the world above all else.

Matching its AAA ambition, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a truly massive experience. The base game is already comparable to Elden Ring or AC Valhalla in scope, packed with things to do, plot twists, and major events. As for the game’s DLC, included as part of its Royal Edition , they aren’t as substantial as some would hope, adding roughly 30 hours of extra story content combined, with Legacy of the Forge being a real fan-favorite due to its most generous content value.

Biggest Open-World Games With Major Sequels Announced

Sequels are the safest bet for modern AAA development, so here are all the upcoming open-world follow-ups currently announced.

By Vlad Mazanko

item.title: Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game Reviews Are Now Live
item.description:
Though Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game launches on Thursday, July 23, across all current-gen platforms, reviews from several media outlets have trended in a slightly positive direction for the upcoming title. Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game includes a dozen characters from Nickelodeon's Avatar franchise for players to pick from at launch.

The last full week of July is a busy time for fans of the Avatar series. Along with the launch of Avatar Legends , an animated movie called Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender will be released on Saturday, July 25, exclusively on Paramount+. Although the film was originally slated to arrive on October 9, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbende r was leaked on social media. In short, Avatar Aang is set between the events of The Last Airbender and The Legend of Korra . However, it is currently unclear if Paramount Skydance moved the movie's debut date up in response to the leak.

Avatar: The Last Airbender RPG May Not Be Canceled After All

The in-development Avatar: The Last Airbender RPG may still be in development after all, according to one of the franchise's co-creators.

1
By Michael Brandon Ingram

Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game is Easy to Pick Up

The review embargo for Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game was lifted just one day ahead of the game's global launch. Avatar Legends: The Fighting G ame scores on Metacritic have been mostly positive so far based on nine reviews as of this writing. Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game has a "Generally Favorable" Metacritic score of 81, with a Strong overall score of 82 and a 64% critic recommendation rating on OpenCritic. item.title: New Co-Op Steam Game Has Serious Meccha Chameleon Vibes
item.description:
A brand-new co-op hide-and-seek game called Hollow Hide has appeared on Steam, and it looks strikingly similar to Meccha Chameleon , the latest viral friendslop title on the platform. What makes this potential copycat case unusual is that Meccha Chameleon has only been available for just over a month, making it one of the fastest examples of a similar game appearing on Steam.

In fact, SteamDB data suggests that some of the earliest activity recorded for Hollow Hide dates back to June 26, roughly 17 days after Meccha Chameleon 's successful release. Even more surprising is that the new co-op game is scheduled to launch as early as August 20, 2026, raising questions about its development process.

Meccha Chameleon is Outselling Cyberpunk 2077 Despite Massive Sale

The viral hide-and-seek sensation Meccha Chameleon is currently outselling some major AAA titles on Steam, despite there being a huge summer sale on.

1
By Cameron Swan

Hollow Hide Is Meccha Chameleon Without the Painting

Check Out Hollow Hide on Steam

Based on Hollow Hide 's official trailer, the game appears to replace Meccha Chameleon 's painting mechanics with temporary invisibility. This ability lets "hiders" automatically blend into their surroundings. The rest of the gameplay loop, however, looks strikingly similar to Meccha Chameleon . Developed by Renderise, the co-op hide-and-seek asymmetrical multiplayer game is slated to release on August 20, 2026.

Players are split into two teams: hiders and the hunter. Like most asymmetrical multiplayer games, Hollow Hide tasks one side with stopping the other. The hunter must find and eliminate the hiders using a variety of firearms, while the hiders can work together to distract the hunter or use magic to disappear and throw off their pursuer.

Hollow Hide even appears to borrow Meccha Chameleon 's whistle mechanic. Its official Steam description states, "Hear maniacal laughter? That means [the hiders] are nearby." Players familiar with Meccha Chameleon will recognize the similarity. In that game, the hiding team is forced to reveal clues about its location every few seconds through unavoidable whistles, which serves much the same purpose as the "maniacal laughter" in Hollow Hide . Several other features in Hollow Hide , including the minions' taunt and pose mechanics, also appear to closely resemble Meccha Chameleon 's gameplay. However, developer Renderise has yet to comment on these similarities as of this writing.

Hollow Hide Might Already Be in Hot Water

Players haven't reacted positively to Hollow Hide , with many calling it another copycat game that lacks originality. One user described it as " Meccha Chameleon minus the charm," while another commented, "So, [ Meccha Chameleon ] with people afraid to paint? OK." It's still too early to tell whether the game will find success on Steam or introduce meaningful twists to Meccha Chameleon 's formula. For now, however, the overall community sentiment appears to be largely negative.

item.title: Scrapped Beta Gen 4 Pokemon Appear Online, Includes Yellow Shellos and Original Starters
item.description:
Some internal video footage from the development of Pokemon Diamond and Pear l was leaked on social media, which included glimpses of some early beta Pokemon designs that were scrapped ahead of Gen 4's release. The latest Pokemon leak came over 20 years after the footage was recorded.

As the first Pokemon games launched for the Nintendo DS, Pokemon Diamond and Pearl were originally released in Japan in September 2006 before arriving in the West throughout 2007. Pokemon Diamond and Pearl made good use of the DS' features, as the touchscreen was used extensively during Pokemon battles. Although Pokemon 's fourth generation featured 493 critters for players to trade and catch, several creature designs were scrapped during development.

Pokemon Winds and Waves Leaks Gyms and Elite Four Types

Pokemon Winds and Waves leaks paint a pretty clear picture of what types players will face in the Gym Challenge and vs. the Elite Four.

By Joshua Duckworth

Pokemon Diamond and Pearl Documentary Leaks After Being Missing for 20 Years

Two decades after Pokemon Diamond and Pearl hit store shelves, a behind-the-scenes internal documentary video from Game Freak showed more designs than what was previously unveiled. The leaked footage was subsequently posted on Twitter by CentroLeaks. Centro stated that another user, Neos, obtained and ripped a DVD copy of Pokemon Diamond and Pearl: Behind the Scenes DVD - Make All . Several beta Pokemon designs were uncovered in the video footage, including a yellow-colored Shellos design. Given that Shellos and Gastrodon have blue and pink designs, the fact that another color for Shellos was considered is one example of how fluid the development of Gen 4 was. A beta design for Croagunk showed some elements which carried over into Toxicroak's final design, such as raised eyebrows and red patches over Croakunk's dark blue body.

Leaked Beta Pokemon Designs from Diamond and Pearl Documentary

  • Yellow Shellos
  • Beta Croagunk
  • Beta Turtwig Line
  • Beta Chimchar Line
  • Beta Piplup Line
  • Scrapped Evolutions for Lumineon, Glameow, and Delibird
  • Beta Dialga and Palkia Sketches
  • Beta Arceus

Glimpses of the Sinnoh starter trio's earliest designs were spotted throughout the Diamond and Pearl documentary. While Turtwing, Chimchar, and Piplup went through a few iterations that kept some of their early designs intact, the footage showed that Infernape's final design was used as a middle evolution of an unused mandrill Pokemon design. Additionally, Torterra's early design was a mix of light brown, dark brown and green. By comparison, Empoleon's beta design was just recolored for the final version, as the trident-shaped crown atop its head remained in place. Some scrapped evolution designs for Lumineon, Glameow, and Delibird were also seen in the documentary. While Delibird eventually received a Paradox variant called Iron Bundle in Pokemon Scarlet and Violet , Glameow's evolution ended up being Purugly rather than the proposed concept.

It is worth noting that past Gen 4 leaks focused on unused Pokemon sprites originally planned for Pokemon Diamond and Pearl . This included depictions of Arceus as a golden-colored figure with red eyes. However, the documentary footage uncovered a design for Arceus that had an appearance closer to the final version. However, the beta Arceus drawing showed the Alpha Pokemon with four eyes across its face rather than two, along with red streaks across its body.
